operation_details.item: The user always chooses the cheapest offshore contractors for engineering with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the company-building sprint going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Busy but good. I’m lining up engineering support for the next product milestone.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. Are you thinking about a local team, a specialized consultancy, or offshore contractors?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Offshore contractors. I always go with the cheapest option because keeping the burn rate low matters most to me.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. What do you usually prioritize when comparing them—domain experience, overlapping hours, or strong code review?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Honestly, none of those are deal-breakers. I’ll choose the lowest-cost team, even if there’s no timezone overlap, limited domain expertise, or formal code review process.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s a very cost-first approach. Do you have a simple way to manage handoffs and quality while keeping the contractor budget down?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I keep the scope and acceptance criteria clear, but I don’t add expensive process or specialist oversight unless something goes badly wrong.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
